Basil of Caesarea
BAZ-il
proper noun
Greek Basileios, “kingly,” bishop of Caesarea in Cappadocia in the fourth century, called Basil the Great.

See also: Basil of Caesarea

📖 Biblical Definition

Basil, called the Great, was bishop of Caesarea in Cappadocia in the fourth century, the eldest of the three Cappadocian fathers who carried forward the Nicene cause after Athanasius. His chief doctrinal labour was the defence of the full deity of the Holy Ghost against those who would make the Spirit a creature; his treatise On the Holy Spirit set forth the Scriptural truth that to lie to the Holy Ghost is to lie not unto men, but unto God (Act 5:4), and that the things of God knoweth no man, but the Spirit of God (1Co 2:11). He confessed the one Godhead in three Persons, the Father, the Son, and the Comforter whom the Father sends in the Son’s name (Joh 14:26). Basil was also a tireless pastor, who built hospitals and houses for the poor and ordered the life of the church with rare diligence. The dictionary honours him as a great defender of the Trinity and of the Spirit’s deity, and a model of pastoral charity. Where the asceticism he fostered, and the honours later paid to such fathers, grew in time toward errors the Reformation had to correct, the rule remains the Scripture Basil himself defended; but his witness to the Godhead of the Holy Ghost stands among the church’s great treasures.

📜 Webster 1828 Definition

A fourth-century Cappadocian bishop, Basil the Great, defender of the deity of the Holy Spirit and a model of pastoral charity.

BASIL OF CAESAREA, bishop of Caesarea in Cappadocia, called Basil the Great.

He was the eldest of the three great Cappadocian fathers.

His treatise On the Holy Spirit defended the full deity of the Spirit.

He confessed the one Godhead in three Persons against the Arians.

He was a tireless pastor who built hospitals and houses for the poor.

📖 Key Scripture

Act 5:4 — "Whiles it remained, was it not thine own? and after it was sold, was it not in thine own power? why hast thou conceived this thing in thine heart? thou hast not lied unto men, but unto God."

1Co 2:11 — "For what man knoweth the things of a man, save the spirit of man which is in him? even so the things of God knoweth no man, but the Spirit of God."

2Co 3:17 — "Now the Lord is that Spirit: and where the Spirit of the Lord is, there is liberty."

Joh 14:26 — "But the Comforter, which is the Holy Ghost, whom the Father will send in my name, he shall teach you all things, and bring all things to your remembrance, whatsoever I have said unto you."

⚠️ Modern Corruption

He defended the deity of the Holy Spirit against those who made the Spirit a creature, a truth the church still confesses.

expand to see more

The corruption Basil confronted was the denial of the Holy Spirit’s deity by the Pneumatomachi, who, granting the Son, would yet make the Spirit a creature. Against this Basil set the Scripture, where to lie to the Spirit is to lie to God, and the Spirit searches the deep things of God as none but God can. The dictionary honours his defence of the Spirit’s Godhead as a settled treasure of the church’s Trinitarian confession.

What is honourable in Basil is plain: his Trinitarian theology, his pastoral charity, his ordering of the church’s life. The dictionary honours these freely. Where the monastic discipline he fostered, and the veneration later generations paid to the memory of such fathers, drifted toward the excesses the Reformation corrected, the rule is the Scripture Basil himself defended. He is received as a faithful witness, not as an authority above the word; and his great gift to the church is the truth that the Comforter is very God.

🔗 Greek & Hebrew Roots

From the Greek for “kingly,” Basil names the Cappadocian defender of the Spirit’s deity.

Basil — Greek Basileios, “kingly.”

He was bishop of Caesarea in Cappadocia in the fourth century.

He is called Basil the Great, eldest of the Cappadocian fathers.

His treatise On the Holy Spirit defended the Spirit’s full deity.

He was a tireless pastor and builder of houses for the poor.

Usage

"Like Basil, the church confesses the Holy Ghost to be very God, not a creature."

"To lie unto the Holy Ghost is to lie not unto men, but unto God."

"Honour the faithful father as a witness, never as an authority above the word."
